what: Established English and Chinese titles for the 95 liturgy texts, with the backend ids each text was uploaded under.
attested: true = the title is used in a published translation or reference work, and `*_source` is where it was found. false = no established title was found and this one was translated for this vault; review before treating it as canonical.

texts.en_title: Khyungpo's Aspiration Prayer
texts.notes: Short dedication/aspiration calling the lamas, yidams, dakinis and dharma protectors to witness the dedication; BDRC bdr:WA0XL70F36EDBCA4C confirms the title 'khyung po'i smon lam' but no author and no published English or Chinese translation found.

texts.en_title: The Threefold Torma Offering
texts.notes: Ritual for offering torma in three portions - to the directional protectors, the elemental spirits (bhuta) and the obstructors - citing the Vajra-arising tantra; the widely circulated Mindroling recension is by Terdak Lingpa. No author given in the record.

texts.en_title: The Prayer Which Removes All Obstacles from the Path
en_alt: The Prayer to Guru Rinpoche that Removes All Obstacles from the Path
Barché Lamsel—The Prayer that Removes All Obstacles from the Path
The Prayer that Dispels All Obstacles from the Path
zh_alt: 蓮花生大士消除障道遂欲成就祈請頌
texts.notes: Barché Lamsel, the outer prayer of the Tukdrub Barché Künsel terma revealed by Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa; incipit (Amitābha/Avalokiteśvara/Padmākara triad plus the twelve manifestations) confirms it. Chinese naming is unsettled — several renderings circulate and I could not pin one canonical URL.

texts.en_title: The Prayer that Swiftly Fulfils All Wishes
en_alt: The Prayer to Guru Rinpoche that Swiftly Fulfils All Wishes
The Prayer that Swiftly Fulfils All Wishes (Sampa Nyur Drupma)
texts.notes: Guru Rinpoche prayer; first verse by Longchen Rabjam (Khandro Yangtik), remaining verses by Jigme Lingpa. Incipit E ma ho / mtsho dbus ge sar confirmed on Lotsawa House.

texts.en_title: The Prayer in Seven Chapters
en_alt: The Prayer in Seven Chapters to Padmakara, the Second Buddha
texts.notes: Padmasambhava terma revealed by Tulku Zangpo Drakpa; the incipit is chapter 1, the prayer to the three-kaya guru.

texts.en_title: Aspiration to be Reborn in the Pure Realm of Sukhāvatī
en_alt: The Aspiration for Sukhāvatī, the Pure Realm of Great Bliss
Karma Chagme's Aspiration Prayer of the Pure Realm of Sukhavati
texts.notes: Karma Chagmé (Rāga Asya) rnam dag bde chen zhing gi smon lam, the most famous Tibetan Sukhāvatī aspiration; incipit e ma ho / 'di nas nyi ma nub kyi phyogs rol na confirms. Chinese 極樂願文 is the standard title (Khenpo Sodargye's translation).

texts.en_title: In Praise of the Miracles
en_alt: Praise of the Great Miracle at Sravasti
Praise of the Buddha's Miraculous Displays
texts.notes: Verse praise by the Kashmiri pandita Sakyasribhadra of the Buddha's fifteen days of miracles, tracing his journey from Rajagriha through Vaishali, Kaushambi and elsewhere to Sravasti; recited during Chotrul Duchen. BDRC confirms the Tibetan title cho 'phrul gyi bstod pa; no published English or Chinese title found, both titles are my renderings.

texts.en_title: The Tea Offering: The Crown Jewel
en_alt: A Tea Offering Called The Jewel of the Crown
texts.notes: Tea-offering (ja mchod) liturgy by Drikung Chungtsang I Rigdzin Chokyi Drakpa; incipit offers tea as amrita to the 'utterly pure crown jewel' deity. No English or Chinese translation found on Lotsawa House, Drikung Translation, Rigpa Wiki or Chinese sites; both titles are my own renderings.

texts.en_title: Great Bliss Samantabhadra: A Tea Offering
en_alt: The Tea Offering Great Bliss Samantabhadra
Tea Offering of Ever-Excellent Great Bliss
texts.notes: Tea-offering (ja chö) guru-yoga liturgy named from its opening words bde chen kun bzang; BDRC WA0XLEAFB80EC29C0 confirms the Tibetan title but no English or Chinese rendering exists, so both titles are my translations.

texts.en_title: Praise to Lord Atisha
en_alt: A Praise to Jowo Je Atisha
Praise to Lord Atisha, the 'Phunsum Tsokpa-ma
Praise to Atisha Beginning 'In the Excellent Land
texts.notes: Short praise/supplication to Atisha Dipamkara, known by its opening words 'phun sum tshogs pa'; BDRC WA0XL9DAEBC6BA92B confirms the title. The opening quatrain is attested in Chinese at amrtf.org as 富饒之地邦伽羅／貴冑撒賀王種姓／菩薩靜命所生族／燃燈智足敬頂禮, but no titled English or Chinese edition found. Distinct from Nagtso Lotsawa's Eighty Verses of Praise, which opens differently.

texts.en_title: Prayer to the Successive Incarnations of the Tai Situ
en_alt: Prayer to the Successive Rebirths of the Tai Situpas
Supplication to the Tai Situ Incarnation Line
zh_alt: 泰錫度歷代轉世祈請文
大司徒仁波切轉世祈請文
texts.notes: Skye phreng gsol 'debs for the Kenting Tai Situ line; BDRC title 'tA yi si tu rim par byon pa rnams la gsol ba 'debs pa'. Opening verses supplicate Wangchuk Dorje and Chöying Dorje (9th and 10th Karmapas), consistent with authorship by the 5th Situ Chökyi Gyaltsen (1586-1657). No published translation found.

texts.en_title: Praise of the Buddha
en_alt: Great Praise of the Twelve Acts of the Buddha
Praise by Way of the Twelve Deeds
texts.notes: Nagarjuna's praise of the Buddha's twelve acts, prefaced by the homage verse Tabkhe Tukje Ma traditionally credited to Drikung Kyobpa Jikten Sumgon - which explains the record's author field. Full Tibetan title thub pa'i bstod pa thabs mkhas thugs rje ma.

texts.en_title: Benefiting Beings Pervading Space: The Meditation and Recitation of the Great Compassionate One
en_alt: For the Benefit of Beings Pervading Space
texts.zh_title: 利生遍空大悲觀世音菩薩修誦儀軌
zh_alt: 利生遍空觀音菩薩成就法
遍空利生大悲觀音修誦儀軌
texts.notes: Thangtong Gyalpo's four-armed Avalokiteśvara sādhana, the standard Kagyu Chenrezig practice; incipit (refuge verse then HRĪḤ on lotus and moon at the crown) matches.

texts.en_title: Short Praise of the Buddha's Deeds
en_alt: Praise of the Twelve Deeds of Buddha Shakyamuni
In Praise of the Buddha's Twelve Deeds
zh_alt: 釋迦牟尼佛十二相成道讚
texts.notes: Praise of Sakyamuni's twelve deeds by Aryasura (slob dpon dpa' bo); Tibetan title on Lotsawa House matches the stem exactly. Chinese title not confirmed against a source.

texts.en_title: In Praise of the Buddha: Though All Sages Are Equal in Abandonment and Realization
en_alt: In Praise of the Buddha's Twelve Deeds
zh_alt: 釋迦牟尼佛十二事業讚
texts.notes: Fifth Dalai Lama's praise of Sakyamuni structured on the twelve deeds (Tusita descent, white-elephant conception, etc.); no published English or Chinese title found.

texts.en_title: In Praise of the Twelve Deeds of the Buddha
en_alt: In Praise of the Twelve Acts of the Buddha
texts.zh_title: 世尊佛陀十二相佛行讚頌
texts.notes: Nāgārjuna's Dvādaśakāranāmastotra (mdzad pa bcu gnyis kyi tshul la bstod pa); the liturgy prefixes the four-line thabs mkhas thugs rje homage, which is why BDRC labels the work thub pa'i bstod pa thabs mkhas thugs rje ma. Second verse gang gis dang por byang chub thugs bskyed nas matches the canonical opening (Chinese 誰從最初發起菩提心).

texts.en_title: The Sage's Harmonious Song of Truth: A Prayer for the Flourishing of the Non-Sectarian Teachings of the Buddha
en_alt: Prayer for the Flourishing of the Non-Sectarian Teachings of the Buddha
texts.zh_title: 佛陀聖教無偏興盛祈願文
zh_alt: 仙人諦語妙音——佛陀聖教無偏興盛祈願文
texts.notes: Rime aspiration composed by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1999 at Trulshik Rinpoche's request; full Tibetan title thub bstan ris med rgyas pa'i smon lam drang srong bden pa'i dbyangs snyan. Incipit verified against Lotsawa House. Chinese title is my rendering.

texts.en_title: A Prayer for the Beginning, Middle, and End of Practice
en_alt: The Prayer of the Virtuous Beginning, Middle and End
A Prayer for the Beginning, Middle and End
texts.notes: Tsongkhapa's aspiration prayer; FPMT edition prints the identical Tibetan title page (thog mtha' ma). Chinese version by Shi Faju matches the homage and first verse exactly.

texts.en_title: The Hundred Deities of Tushita
en_alt: The Hundred Deities of the Land of Joy
The Guru Yoga of Tushita's Deva Host
zh_alt: 宗喀巴大師上師瑜伽法
texts.notes: The standard Lama Tsongkhapa guru yoga; this recension adds the fulfilment-requests and aspiration prayers by Könchok Jigme Wangpo, which the established titles do not name.

texts.en_title: Gelongma Palmo's Praise of Avalokiteshvara
zh_alt: 帕摩比丘尼所造聖觀自在讚
texts.notes: The famous 'po praise' (every line ends in -po) recited in the Nyungne fasting retreat, attributed to Bhikshuni Lakshmi / Gelongma Palmo; Sanskrit Aryavalokitesvarastotra (BDRC WA0RT1550, rKTs WTT1550). BDRC's ATII attribution names Candragomin and the colophon of this print names dge slong ma zla mdzes, so authorship in the canon is contested even though liturgical use credits Gelongma Palmo. No titled Chinese edition located.

texts.en_title: The Supplement to the Single Intention
en_alt: The Supplementary Vajra Statements of the Single Intention
texts.notes: Drikung Kagyu: the lhan thabs (supplementary vajra statements) appended to Jigten Sumgön's Gongchig / Single Intention; homage is to 'Drikung Rinchen'. 'Single Intention' is the established English for dgongs gcig (Sobisch, Wisdom 2020), but no attested title for the lhan thabs itself. Incipit counts forty supplements, while the standard Gongchig is described as having forty-six.

texts.en_title: Essence of the Two Accumulations
en_alt: Essence of the Two Accumulations: The Ritual for the Elaborate Outer Practice from the Mind Treasure Tara's Profound Essence
The Mandala Ritual, Essence of the Two Accumulations
texts.zh_title: 供獻曼達集積二資糧之心要儀軌
zh_alt: 度母甚深心髓二資糧心要儀軌
texts.notes: Tara ritual from the mind treasure Tara's Profound Essence (Zabtik Drolchok); incipit matches Lotsawa House's elaborate outer-practice version verbatim. Two caveats: Lotsawa House attributes the cycle to Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (arranged by Jamgon Kongtrul), not Jigme Lingpa as in the record; and the record's heading reads mandala ritual where Lotsawa House has outer-practice ritual, so this may be a distinct mandala-offering recension.

texts.en_title: A Daily Practice of the Meditation and Recitation of Glorious Guhyasamāja
texts.zh_title: 吉祥密集金剛修誦日修儀軌
texts.notes: Akṣobhyavajra-Guhyasamāja daily sādhana by Zava Damdin Losang Tamdin (BDRC P1638); no established English or Chinese title found, both fields are my own translations. BDRC gives 密集金刚 as the Chinese for Guhyasamāja.

texts.en_title: A Prayer to Kindle the Three Kinds of Faith Addressed to the Seventeen Great Paṇḍitas of Glorious Nālandā
en_alt: Illuminating the Threefold Faith: An Invocation of the Seventeen Great Paṇḍitas of Glorious Nālandā
Prayer to the Seventeen Nalanda Masters
A Prayer to Kindle the Three Kinds of Faith: The 17 Nalanda Panditas
texts.zh_title: 那爛陀寺十七大班智達祈請文
zh_alt: 至高那難陀寺十七大班智達祈請文·能明三信
至高那爛陀寺十七大班智達之顯明三信祈請文
那爛陀寺十七大班智達祈願文
texts.notes: By the 14th Dalai Lama, 2001; full Tibetan title ends dad gsum gsal byed. Stem has paN grub for the usual paN chen.

texts.en_title: The Glorious Three Realms: A Supplication to Je Tsongkhapa
en_alt: Sole Eye of the Beings of the Three Realms
Verses on the Glorious Three Realms
zh_alt: 宗喀巴大師略傳·吉祥三界頌
宗喀巴祈禱文：吉祥三界篇
texts.notes: Khedrup Je's verse supplication recounting Tsongkhapa's life; Chinese 吉祥三界頌 matches the incipit line for line. No English translation found.

texts.en_title: Words to Delight the Guru Mañjughoṣa: A Prayer of Aspiration for the Flourishing and Spread of the Glorious Sakya Teachings
en_alt: Aspiration for the Flourishing of the Glorious Sakya Teachings: Words to Delight the Guru Mañjughoṣa
Prayer for the Spread and Flourishing of the Sakya Teachings
texts.zh_title: 薩迦教法弘揚廣布祈願文——令文殊上師歡喜之教言
texts.notes: Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö; BDRC WA0XLA163F92DC91C confirms the Tibetan title and author. No published English or Chinese translation found — Lotsawa House's two Sakya-flourishing texts by the same author (sakya-invocation, prayer-to-sakya-scholars) are different works. Titles here are my own renderings. Rendering follows Lotsawa House's convention for dgyes pa'i zhal lung titles (cf. Words to Delight the Lake-Born One).

texts.en_title: The Great Cloud of Blessings: The Prayer which Magnetizes All that Appears and Exists
en_alt: Wangdü: The Great Cloud of Blessings
zh_alt: 現有自在攝受祈禱文——大加持雲
texts.notes: Mipham Rinpoche's 1879 magnetizing prayer, full title snang srid dbang du sdud pa'i gsol 'debs byin rlabs sprin chen; incipit om ah hung hrih / bde chen 'bar ba dbang gi pho brang du verified.

texts.en_title: Praise of Sarasvatī
en_alt: Praise of Sarasvatī, Goddess of Eloquence
In Praise of the Goddess Sarasvatī
texts.notes: Tsongkhapa's famous praise; full Tibetan title sgra dbyangs lha mo dbyangs can ma la bstod pa. Incipit (white clouds / lightning garlands / gandharva maidens) matches Lotsawa House exactly. Chinese title 妙音天女讚 is standard (Tibetan-recitation series pair it with this exact Tibetan title) but no stable canonical URL was captured.

texts.en_title: Migtsema: A Prayer to Jé Tsongkhapa
texts.notes: The five-line praise-prayer to Tsongkhapa; authorship alternates in the tradition between Tsongkhapa himself and his teacher Rendawa (the input credits Rendawa).

texts.en_title: Supplication to the Life of the First Karmapa, Dusum Khyenpa
en_alt: Supplication to the Life Story of Dusum Khyenpa
Praise to the Life of Dusum Khyenpa
zh_alt: 第一世噶瑪巴杜松虔巴祈請文
texts.notes: Verse supplication to the life story of the First Karmapa Dusum Khyenpa by the Eighth Karmapa Mikyo Dorje; incipit 'Emaho... mtshur phu pa la gsol ba 'debs' matches the published translation exactly. BDRC WA0XLA5CF03B52291 titles it rje dus gsum mkhyen pa la gsol ba btab pa. Chinese title is my rendering; 杜松虔巴 is the Karmapa office (Taiwan) spelling, 都松欽巴 the PRC one.

texts.en_title: Sang Offering to Kurukullā
en_alt: A Sang Offering to the Padma Ḍākinī Kurukullā: The Lotus Net
texts.zh_title: 蓮花空行作明佛母煨桑供養‧蓮花網
texts.notes: Mipham Rinpoche's sang (purificatory smoke) offering to the magnetizing dakini Kurukulla, written for the physician Atsang; Lotsawa House match confirmed by the ram yam kham opening and the fragrant-wood instruction. Chinese deity name 作明佛母 is standard but the full title is my own rendering.

texts.en_title: The Hundred Verses of Advice to the People of Tingri
en_alt: Advice to the People of Tingri
zh_alt: 覺悟者的臨終贈言：定日百法
texts.notes: Padampa Sangye's final testament to the people of Tingri, each verse ending in the vocative ding ri ba; standard English edition is the Padmakara/Shambhala translation with Dilgo Khyentse's commentary.

texts.en_title: Prayer to the Mahāmudrā Lineage
en_alt: Supplication to the Mahāmudrā Lineage Gurus
zh_alt: 大手印上師傳承祈請文
texts.notes: Gelug (Ganden Kagyü) Mahāmudrā lineage supplication by the First Panchen Lama Losang Chökyi Gyaltsen — opens NAMO MAHĀMUDRĀYE and supplicates Vajradhara with a repeating four-line blessing refrain. 'Mahamudra Lineage Prayer' / 大手印傳承祈請文 are in circulation but usually denote the Kagyu Dorje Chang Thungma, so both are flagged unattested for this text.

texts.en_title: The Abridged Chronicle
texts.notes: Terma-punctuated condensed Padma Kathang recounting Guru Rinpoche's successive births; opens with the Oddiyana-language homage buddha dharma sangha ya. No established English or Chinese title found.

texts.en_title: The Secret Pith Instruction for Averting Maras
en_alt: Secret Instruction for Repelling Demonic Forces
texts.notes: Short Mipham verse instruction on recognising and averting mara-influences; authorship confirmed via BDRC (creator P252, Ju Mipham). Absent from Lotsawa House's Mipham and 'Averting Obstacles' indexes, so both titles are my own renderings.

texts.en_title: Brief Sukhāvatī Aspiration
texts.notes: Namchö terma revealed by Tertön Mingyur Dorje, spoken by Amitābha in 1657; incipit e ma ho / ngo mtshar sangs rgyas snang ba mtha' yas dang confirmed against Lotsawa House. Attributed here to Rāga Asya (Karma Chagmé), who recorded Mingyur Dorje's revelations. Chinese title is my own rendering. Chinese circles refer to the Namchö Sukhāvatī aspiration as 天法極樂願文 (天法 = Namchö), but I could not verify that name against this text's opening lines, so it is listed only as an alternative.

texts.en_title: The Prayer of the Words of Truth
texts.notes: The 14th Dalai Lama's 1960 prayer written shortly after arriving in exile, opening namo ratna trayaya; English title verified on Lotsawa House and dalailama.com. No attested Chinese title located, zh_title is my rendering.

texts.en_title: The Prayer to Guru Rinpoche that Spontaneously Fulfils All Wishes
en_alt: The Prayer that Spontaneously Fulfils All Wishes
texts.zh_title: 願望任運自然成就祈請頌
zh_alt: 蓮師意樂任運成就祈請文
texts.notes: Chapter 7 of the Le'u Dunma terma revealed by Tulku Zangpo Drakpa (record credits Padmasambhava, the speaker). Incipit 'nub phyogs bde ba can gyi zhing khams su' matches both the Lotsawa House and Chinese versions.

texts.en_title: A Concise Dedication and Aspiration
en_alt: A Brief Dedication and Aspiration Prayer
texts.notes: Short dedication-and-aspiration by Golok Serta Rinpoche Pema Lungtok Gyatso (1891–1964, BDRC P731); Lotsawa House carries only two of his texts and not this one, so both titles are my translations.

texts.en_title: Prayer for the Future of the Dharma
en_alt: Prayer for the Flourishing of the Teachings
texts.notes: Popular aspiration opening with homage to the seven buddhas and the refrain 'may the teachings blaze'; first verse from the Pratimoksa-sutra, the rest from Atisha's Mahasutrasamuccaya. Chinese verses are canonical, drawn from 《大方等大集月藏經．法滅盡品》 ('令法久熾然'); 聖教熾燃願 is the standard Tibetan-tradition Chinese title.

texts.en_title: Prayer for Peace and Stability in Tibet
en_alt: Prayer for the Wellbeing of Tibet
Aspiration for the Happiness of Tibet
texts.notes: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé; Lotsawa House Tibetan page reproduces the identical first four lines (skyabs gnas bslu med dkon mchog rtsa ba gsum). No Chinese version located.

texts.en_title: Exhorting the Protectors of Tibet
en_alt: Exhorting the Guardian Deities, Protectors of Tibet, to Act
An Invocation of the Guardian Deities of Tibet
zh_alt: 祈請護藏神眾行持事業文
texts.notes: HH the 14th Dalai Lama's exhortation to the local deities and guardians of Tibet; the record's opening kye ma rmad is an orthographic variant of Lotsawa House's kyai ma smad. No Chinese title found in circulation - the Chinese given is a rendering.

texts.en_title: The Bodhisattva's Confession of Downfalls
en_alt: Confession of a Bodhisattva's Downfalls to the Thirty-Five Buddhas
The Bodhisattva's Confession of Moral Downfalls
The Sūtra of the Three Heaps (Triskandha-sūtra)
zh_alt: 佛說三十五佛名禮懺文
texts.notes: Buddhavacana (from the Upāliparipṛcchā), the Thirty-Five Buddhas confession; the Lotsawa House Nyingma recension matches the incipit's 'all sentient beings take refuge in the guru' phrasing. Classical Chinese equivalent is Amoghavajra's T.326.

texts.en_title: Aspiration for the Building of a Maitreya Statue
en_alt: Prayer for Those who Help Erect an Image of Maitreya
texts.notes: Aspiration by Gyalwa Gendun Drup (First Dalai Lama), who built the great Maitreya at Tashilhunpo; dedicates merit of those who provide conditions for erecting a Maitreya statue. No attested title found.

texts.en_title: The Noble Maitreya's King of Aspirations
en_alt: The King of Aspirational Prayers of Arya Maitreya
texts.zh_title: 佛說彌勒菩薩發願王偈
texts.notes: Arya-maitri-pranidhana-raja (BDRC WA4CZ32863), Toh 1096 / Toh 4378; Taisho 1144, rendered from Tibetan by Gombojab in 1743 and matching the incipit exactly.

texts.en_title: The Dhāraṇī that Pacifies the Fifteen Great Grahas that Harm Children
en_alt: The Dhāraṇī for Pacifying the Fifteen Great Harmful Spirits of Children
texts.zh_title: 佛說護諸童子陀羅尼經
zh_alt: 佛說護諸童子陀羅尼咒經
texts.notes: Dhāraṇī opening with homage to Mahāsāhasrapramardanī (stong chen mo rab tu 'joms ma), then Brahmā requesting the vidyā-mantra that benefits children; BDRC WA0XL6D5D3DB61520 confirms the Tibetan title. The Chinese title given is the canonical parallel T1028A (Bodhiruci), which teaches the same fifteen child-afflicting grahas — not a translation of this Tibetan title. English title is my own rendering.

texts.en_title: The Little Hundred Thousand for Children
en_alt: An Unmistaken Condensation of the Meaning of the Noble Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines
texts.notes: Condensed digest of the Satasahasrika Prajnaparamita; BDRC W3CN1595 gives the variant titles 'bum chung, byis pa'i 'bum chung and shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa stong phrag brgya pa'i don ma nor bar bsdus pa, and says it was spread by Atisha and scribed by Balpo Asu. Neither an English nor a Chinese title is attested; both are my renderings.

texts.en_title: Calling the Guru from Afar
en_alt: Calling the Guru from Afar: A Supplication to Pierce Your Heart with Devotion
texts.notes: Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Thaye's bla ma rgyang 'bod kyi gsol 'debs mos gus snying gi gzer 'debs; incipit 'bla ma mkhyen no' matches. English subtitle is variously rendered ('pierce your heart with devotion', 'a nail driven into the heart of devotion').

texts.en_title: Eight Verses of Training the Mind
en_alt: Eight Verses for Training the Mind
texts.notes: The classic Kadampa lojong text by Geshe Langri Thangpa Dorje Sengge (1054–1123); title and text both securely attested.

texts.en_title: Praise to Khedrup Je: The Unrivalled Lion's Roar
en_alt: A Praise of Khedrup Je Gelek Palzang
texts.notes: Praise to Khedrup Je Gelek Palzang (1385-1438) by the Second Dalai Lama Gendun Gyatso; BDRC WA0XL0D85FBF9D96D gives the full title mkhas grub rje'i bstod pa zla bral seng ge'i nga ro, matching the incipit's 'unrivalled in roaring the lion's roar' and the Shambhala Kalki-lineage verse. No published English or Chinese translation found; both titles are my renderings.

texts.en_title: Praise to the Six-Armed Mahākāla
en_alt: Praise to the Swift-Acting Six-Armed Protector
texts.notes: Praise to Six-Armed Mahakala known by its opening words myur mdzad ma; Chinese 六臂怙主讚 matches line for line (恭敬頂禮速救觀世音／腳踏毗那夜迦佩足鐲／身著虎皮下裙大黑天／六臂為諸蛇飾所莊嚴). Attribution to the 2nd Dalai Lama is as given in the source file and was not independently verified.

texts.en_title: Thirty-Seven Point Maṇḍala Offering
texts.notes: The long 37-heap mandala offering (om vajra bhumi ah hum ...), traditionally ascribed to Chogyal Pakpa Lodro Gyaltsen; Tibetan title mandala so bdun ma. Used across all schools; the record gives no author.

texts.en_title: Light Offering Prayer
texts.notes: Lamp/light offering aspiration by Dezhung Tulku Ajam (A jam sprul sku Kunga Gyaltsen); incipit matches the Lotsawa House text. Both 'Light Offering Prayer' and 供燈祈願文 are generic marme-mönlam titles shared by several different texts (Atiśa's being the best known), so they do not uniquely identify this one.

texts.en_title: Averting and Reversing Gossip
texts.notes: Ritual for averting mi kha (harm from gossip/slander); BDRC MW8LS67151 confirms this text sits in a volume with sdig bshags gser gyi spu gri and rgya nag skag bzlog. No established English or Chinese title.

texts.en_title: The Three Praises to the Swift-Acting Protector
texts.notes: Incipit is Shavaripa's praise of six-armed Mahakala (attested English 'Praise of Six-Arm Lord Mahakala', tr. Martin Willson, kurukulla.org); BDRC catalogues the work only as 'myur mdzad ma' (WA0XLEAD8C71390D7), so what the 'rnam gsum' triad comprises is unverified.

texts.en_title: The Four Immeasurables
texts.notes: The standard four-line tshad med bzhi prayer (loving kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity) recited at the start of most liturgies; no single author. Both titles are the universally used names for the set.

texts.en_title: The Seven-Line Prayer
en_alt: The Seven Line Prayer to Guru Rinpoche
texts.notes: The root Seven-Line Prayer to Guru Padmasambhava (hung / orgyen yul gyi nubjang tsam), revealed in Guru Chowang's Lama Sangdu; the most widely chanted Guru Rinpoche invocation.

texts.en_title: A Prayer to Be Cared For Throughout All My Lives
en_alt: Being Taken Into Your Care Throughout Successive Lives
A Prayer to Be Held in Your Care in All Future Lives
texts.notes: Short prayer by the 6th Tseten Zhabdrung Jigme Rigpe Lodro (1910-1985); rjes 'dzin = to take/keep under one's care. No English or Chinese translation found; both titles are my own renderings.

texts.en_title: A Prayer Invoking the Benefits of the Festival of the Tenth Day
texts.notes: Jigme Lingpa's prayer on why the tenth day is dedicated to Guru Padmasambhava and the merit of recalling his twelve deeds; English confirmed on Lotsawa House, Chinese title is my translation.

texts.en_title: Accomplishing Immortality: A Prayer for Long Life
en_alt: A Long-Life Prayer entitled Accomplishing Immortality
zh_alt: 祈請長久住世文‧成就無死
texts.notes: Long-life (zhabs brtan) prayer; author given as Jigme Trinle Gyatso, i.e. Alak Lokho Jigme Trinle Gyatso (b. 1866) of Labrang Tashikhyil, teacher of the Ninth and Tenth Panchen Lamas. The epithets kun gzigs and snang ba mtha' yas suggest the subject is a Panchen Lama, but the addressee is not named in the incipit. Only one witness in BDRC (W3MS261 vol. 14); no translation in either language, both titles are mine.

texts.en_title: The Long-Life Prayer 'In the Blissful Realm of the West
en_alt: Prayer for Long Life Beginning 'Nubchok Deden
texts.notes: Zhabs brtan (long-life supplication) named after its opening words, ascribed to the Nechung Dharma King (the Dalai Lama's state oracle); BDRC confirms the title 'zhabs brtan nub phyogs bde ldan'. The master addressed is styled mchog sprul mthong ba don ldan and cares for 'the teachings and beings of the Land of Snows' — most likely the Dalai Lama, but the identification is not certain.

texts.en_title: The Essence of Practice: Advice That Benefits at the Time of Death
en_alt: Essence of Practice: Instructions Beneficial at the Moment of Death
The Heart of Practice: Advice for the Time of Death
texts.zh_title: 臨終饒益教授：修持心要
zh_alt: 臨終利益之教言：實修心要
臨終饒益教言修持精要
texts.notes: Amitabha / Sukhavati-oriented advice for the moment of death by Tseten Zhabdrung Jigme Rigpe Lodro (才旦夏茸·久美柔貝洛珠, 1910-1985). Author identity confirmed, but no published English or Chinese title found - both titles are my translations.

texts.en_title: Great Perfection Mañjuśrī
en_alt: The Self-Radiance of Indestructible Awareness and Emptiness: An Aspiration towards the Meaning of the Indivisible Ground, Path and Fruition of the Great Perfection Mañjuśrī
texts.zh_title: 文殊大圆满基道果无别发愿文
zh_alt: 文殊大圓滿基道果無別發願文
texts.notes: Mipham's 1886 Dzogchen aspiration; full title is 'jam dpal rdzogs pa chen po'i gzhi lam 'bras bu dbyer med pa'i don la smon pa rig stong rdo rje'i rang gdangs. Incipit verified line-for-line against Lotsawa House. Chinese title given verbatim (simplified) as published; traditional variant in zh_alt.

texts.en_title: The Praise to Mañjuśrī—Glorious Wisdom's Excellent Qualities
texts.notes: The famous Gang lo ma by Vajrayudha (rdo rje mtshon cha); formal Tibetan title dpal ye shes yon tan bzang po zhes bya ba'i bstod pa, Tengyur Toh 2711.

texts.en_title: The Mind Training Induced by Way of Poem, A Perfect Composition of Words
en_alt: Mind Training Adorned with Poetic Sound Ornaments
A Poetic Mind Training with Ornaments of Sound
texts.notes: Rare Tsongkhapa lojong in alliterative verse (sgra rgyan = sabdalamkara), confirmed as 'rje tsong kha pa'i gsung blo sbyong snyan ngag sgra rgyan' (BDRC W8LS76593); English title comes from a single Dharma-centre course listing.

texts.en_title: A Shower of Benefit and Happiness: Praise and Supplication to Noble Avalokiteśvara
en_alt: Praise and Supplication to Noble Avalokiteśvara: A Shower of Benefit and Happiness
Raining Down Benefit and Bliss: A Praise and Prayer to the Great Compassionate One
texts.zh_title: 聖大悲觀音讚頌祈請文·降澍利樂雨
texts.notes: Seventh Dalai Lama Kelsang Gyatso; BDRC WA0XLDEB6DFF1A465 confirms the Tibetan title, and the incipit namo āryalokiśvarāya fits. No English or Chinese translation found (not on Lotsawa House, which holds only one Seventh Dalai Lama text). Both titles are my own renderings.

texts.en_title: The Noble Sūtra of Recalling the Three Jewels
en_alt: The Sūtra Remembering the Three Jewels
The Recollection of the Three Jewels
texts.notes: Kangyur sutra (Toh 279-281) reciting the qualities of Buddha, Dharma and Sangha; incipit matches the Chinese 頂禮一切智智尊／如是佛陀薄伽梵者 (法尊法師 translation). Note the Tibetan heading in the source file has a stray གྱི (rjes su dran pa'i gyi mdo).

texts.en_title: Verses of the Eight Noble Auspicious Ones
en_alt: The Verses for the Eight Auspicious Ones
Verses for the Eight Auspicious Noble Ones
texts.notes: Record credits Buddha Shakyamuni, but the incipit 'snang srid rnam dag rang bzhin lhun grub pa'i' is Mipham Rinpoche's 1896 verses, composed after the Sutra of the Eight Noble Auspicious Ones (Toh 278). Lotsawa House Chinese page titles it 聖八吉祥之文句; 八吉祥頌 / 八聖吉祥頌 are the more common Chinese names.

texts.en_title: The King of Aspiration Prayers: Samantabhadra's Aspiration to Good Actions
zh_alt: 大方廣佛華嚴經普賢行願品
texts.notes: Bhadracaryapranidhanaraja from the Gandavyuha of the Avatamsaka; the Tibetan here is the verse text alone (Toh 1095), whose exact Chinese counterpart is Amoghavajra's 普賢菩薩行願讚 (T0297), though 普賢行願品 is the name in common use.

texts.en_title: The Name Mantra of Noble Avalokiteshvara
en_alt: Praise and Mantra of Noble Avalokiteshvara
Homage and Six-Syllable Mantra of Avalokiteshvara
zh_alt: 觀自在禮讚與六字大明咒
texts.notes: A liturgical unit, not an independent work: the well-known quatrain 'Your thousand arms are the thousand universal monarchs, your thousand eyes the thousand buddhas of this fortunate age...' followed by OM MANI PADME HUM. The quatrain itself is attested in English on Lotsawa House inside Jigme Lingpa's Simple Fasting Ritual, but the heading 'mtshan sngags' has no established English or Chinese title.

texts.en_title: The Seven Branches
en_alt: The Seven Branches from Samantabhadra's Aspiration to Good Actions
texts.notes: The seven-branch practice extracted from the Zangchö Mönlam (Samantabhadra's Aspiration to Good Actions, Bhadracaryapranidhana); incipit ji snyed su dag phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten na = 所有十方世界中，三世一切人師子. BDRC bdr:WA0RT0751 gives the title yan lag bdun pa.

texts.en_title: The Foundation of All Good Qualities
zh_alt: 菩提道次第功德之本頌
texts.notes: Tsongkhapa's fourteen-verse lamrim prayer; the Chinese liturgical text 功德之本頌 opens 能成眾德之體具恩師, matching the incipit exactly.

texts.en_title: Mountain Smoke Offering
texts.notes: Lhatsün Namkha Jikmé's sang offering from the Rigdzin Sokdrub. The incipit begins BHRŪṂ, i.e. this is the terma root text, not Dudjom Rinpoche's expanded 'arranged for recitation' version (which opens oṃ svasti).

texts.en_title: The 'Chinese' Practice of Averting Periodic Obstacles
en_alt: The Chinese Way of Repelling Disaster (rgya nag skag bzlog)
texts.notes: Dharani spoken by Manjushri, from the gzungs bsdus; Tibetan title on Lotsawa House matches the stem exactly. Chinese title not attested.

texts.en_title: In Praise of the Six Ornaments and Two Supreme Ones
en_alt: Praise to the Six Ornaments and the Two Excellent Ones
texts.notes: Praise of Nagarjuna, Asanga et al.; 'Six Ornaments and Two Supreme Ones' is the standard English term but no translation of this praise was found. Note the Chinese 二勝六莊嚴讚 published by amrtf.org is attributed to Tsongkhapa, not Rendawa.

texts.en_title: Aspiration for the Country's Welfare
en_alt: Aspiration for the Happiness of the Realm
texts.notes: Fifteenth Karmapa Khakhyab Dorje; Lotsawa House confirms both the Tibetan title rgyal khams bde ba'i smon lam and the opening Vajra Guru mantra followed by 'gro ba'i skyabs mgon o rgyan rin po che. Chinese title is my own rendering.

texts.en_title: The Name Mantra of Buddha Amitāyus
en_alt: The Name-Mantra of the Conqueror Amitāyus
texts.notes: A single homage verse to Amitayus (jikten drenpe tsowo tsepakme) followed by om amarani jivantiye svaha, from the mtshan sngags name-mantra genre. The verse itself is attested in Trulshik Rinpoche's compilation on Lotsawa House (Buddha of Infinite Life, foremost guide for beings in this world...), but no standalone English or Chinese title for this piece is attested.

texts.en_title: A Praise to Longchen Rabjam, Lord of the Victorious Ones
en_alt: In Praise of Longchen Rabjam, Sovereign of the Victorious Ones
texts.notes: Listed as (klong chen rab 'byams la bstod pa) in the Collection of Praises, vol. 1 of Dodrupchen III Jigme Tenpe Nyima's Collected Works, with no English translation recorded (rigpawiki.org/index.php?title=Dodrupchen_Jikme_Tenpe_Nyima%27s_Collected_Works). Opens with homage to Manjushri. Both titles are my own renderings; 龍欽饒絳 is the standard Chinese for Longchen Rabjam.

texts.en_title: Lama Tsongkhapa's Secret Biography
en_alt: The Secret Biography of Je Tsongkhapa
Prayer of the Secret Biography of Je Tsongkhapa
texts.zh_title: 宗喀巴大師密傳祈請文
zh_alt: 至尊宗喀巴大師密傳祈請文
texts.notes: Verse prayer recounting Tsongkhapa's visionary life, by Jamyang Chöje Tashi Palden (1379–1449), founder of Drepung; the Kurukulla edition gives exactly this Tibetan title and author.

texts.en_title: In Praise of Dependent Origination
en_alt: The Essence of Eloquence: In Praise of the Buddha for Teaching Profound Dependent Arising
Praise to the Buddha for Teaching Dependent Arising
zh_alt: 由說甚深緣起門中稱讚無上大師世尊善說心藏
texts.notes: Je Tsongkhapa's 58-verse praise of the Buddha for teaching dependent origination. Fazun's Chinese translation (CBETA B0052) matches the incipit line for line: 敬禮尊重妙音菩薩／由見說何法，智說成無上，勝者見緣起，垂教我敬禮.

texts.en_title: Smoke Offering for Raising Windhorse
texts.notes: Sang/lhasang offering to buddhas, gurus, dakinis, dharma protectors and wealth deities asking them to support the flourishing of windhorse; ascribed to Rigdzin Chenpo Rigpé Dorje, whom I could not identify with confidence. No published translation found; titles are my own.

texts.en_title: The Three Principal Aspects of the Path
en_alt: Three Principal Aspects of the Path
texts.notes: Tsongkhapa's verse summary of renunciation, bodhicitta and the correct view, composed 1398 as a letter to Ngawang Drakpa.

texts.en_title: Aspiration for the Stages of the Path
en_alt: Prayer for the Stages of the Path
texts.notes: Tsongkhapa's fourteen-stanza lamrim aspiration; incipit verified against Lotsawa House. The Chinese opening 長期勤奮二資糧，積聚廣如虛空者 is an exact match for the same verse, but I could not capture a stable URL for the Chinese text.

texts.en_title: Seven-Branch Praise to the Goddess
texts.notes: Seven-branch (yan lag bdun pa) praise to Palden Lhamo/Shri Devi, opening BHYO dpal ldan lha mo dpag par dka' ba khyod. Author unrecorded in the source metadata.

texts.en_title: The Refuge and Bodhicitta Prayer
texts.notes: The famous four-line refuge and bodhicitta verse; BDRC titles the work skyabs 'gro sems bskyed. Standard Chinese liturgical text is 諸佛正法眾中尊，直至菩提我皈依，我以所行施等善，為利有情願成佛。

texts.en_title: Prayer to Tārā: A Sevenfold Supplication for Protection
texts.notes: Drikung Kyobpa Jigten Sumgön's skyabs bdun ma, composed after a vision of seven forms of Tārā. Incipit ma skye ba med pa'i chos dbyings na matches both the Lotsawa House English and the Chinese 母於無生法界中，安住尊聖之度母.

texts.en_title: Praises to the Twenty-One Tārās
en_alt: Praise to Tārā with Twenty-One Verses of Homage and Their Benefits
In Praise of the Twenty-One Tārās
zh_alt: 聖救度佛母二十一種禮讚經
救度佛母二十一種禮讚經
texts.notes: The canonical Tara praise from the Tara tantra; incipit gives the Sanskrit namas tara ekavimsati stotra guna hita sahita and the Tibetan sgrol ma la phyag 'tshal nyi shu rtsa gcig gis bstod pa phan yon dang bcas pa. Chinese canonical version is T1108B.

texts.en_title: Stairway to Liberation: The Uncommon Guru Yoga in Reliance on Cittamaṇi Tārā
en_alt: Stairway to Liberation: the Uncommon Guru Yoga in Reliance to Cittamaṇi Tārā
texts.zh_title: 依止心寶度母之不共上師瑜伽——趨向解脫之階梯
zh_alt: 心寶度母不共上師瑜伽·解脫階梯
texts.notes: Title and incipit match the Awakening Vajra edition word for word (dag lu tha mal chi wor pe da'i teng...). Authorship differs by source: BDRC WA1KG4594 credits Takphu V Losang Chokyi Wangchuk (as in the record), the published edition credits Panchen Losang Chokyi Gyaltsen. No published Chinese translation found; 心寶度母 is the attested Chinese name for Cittamani Tara.

texts.en_title: Praise to the Teacher, the Lord of Sages
en_alt: In Praise of the Teacher, Lord of Sages
Praise to Our Teacher, the Mighty Sage
texts.notes: Praise to Buddha Shakyamuni by Nyengön Tulku Do-ngak Chökyi Gyatso (1903–1957, BDRC P5425) of Pal Nyenmo Monastery in Golok; only one BDRC instance and no translation on Lotsawa House, so both titles are my translations. Not to be confused with Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö's similarly named Praise of the Lord of Sages.

texts.en_title: The Great Cloud of Blessings: The Prayer which Magnetizes All that Appears and All that Exists
en_alt: Wang Du: The Great Cloud of Blessings
zh_alt: 懷攝顯有祈請文‧加持大雲
texts.notes: Mipham Rinpoche's 1879 magnetizing prayer to the nine magnetizing deities headed by Padma Gyalpo, universally known by its short name Wangdu. Lotsawa House's own Chinese page renders the full title as 懷攝顯有祈請文 名曰加持大雲; 懷業祈禱文 is the form in general Chinese use.

texts.en_title: Aspiration Prayer from the Bodhicharyāvatāra
en_alt: Dedication Prayers from A Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life
zh_alt: 入菩薩行論第十品迴向
texts.notes: Chapter 10 (Dedication) of Shantideva's Bodhicaryavatara recited as a standalone aspiration; incipit is verses 10.1-10.2. Note the source file's fm_title oddly prefixes དམིགས་བརྩེ་མ (Migtsema), which does not belong to this text.

texts.en_title: The Secret Vajra Knot
en_alt: The Secret Vajra Knot: An Aspiration Prayer of the Three Yogas
texts.notes: Terdak Lingpa's popular Nyingma aspiration; full Tibetan title yo ga gsum gyi smon lam rdo rje rgya mdud. Incipit bla ma yi dam lha tshogs dgongs su gsol confirmed against Lotsawa House. No Chinese title found in circulation - the Chinese given is a rendering.

texts.en_title: Yearning Song of Prayer to Invoke the Wisdom Mind of the Compassionate Teacher Padmasambhava
en_alt: A Yearning Song of Prayer to Invoke the Wisdom Mind of the Compassionate Teacher Padmasambhava
texts.zh_title: 悲切啟請大悲上師本誓之祈請文
zh_alt: 策發大悲上師蓮師本誓之悲切祈請文
texts.notes: Composed by HH the 14th Dalai Lama in 1980 at the request of the Kashag, calling on Guru Padmasambhava to honour his pledge to Tibet; incipit verified. No Chinese title found — zh_title is my own translation. Source title spells the verb bskul ba where the vault heading has skul ba.

texts.en_title: The Name Mantra of the Precious Master
en_alt: The Vajra Guru Mantra with its Preliminary Verse
texts.notes: Four-line homage rgya gar pan chen bod la bka' drin che followed by the Vajra Guru mantra OM AH HUM VAJRA GURU PADMA SIDDHI HUM; the same quatrain appears on Lotsawa House as Prayer to Padmasambhava attributed to Menlungpa Mikyo Dorje.

texts.en_title: The Testament Prayer to Orgyen Rinpoche
texts.zh_title: 鄔金仁波切遺教祈請文
zh_alt: 邬金仁波切遗教祈请文
texts.notes: Chokgyur Lingpa terma from the Wish-Fulfilling Tree life-story of Padmasambhava; incipit 'Emaho, dharmakaya Samantabhadra, the sixth Vajradhara' confirmed on both Lotsawa House and Samye Translations.
